reference.label: Transmit laser failure
reference.definition: Hardware failure of a line transmitter laser that removes its optical channel.
reference.example: A 400G transmitter laser stops emitting and the remote receiver loses the channel.

reference.label: Card failure
reference.definition: Card-level hardware failure that removes traffic and monitoring and may mask subordinate alarms.
reference.example: A line card loses power, stops carrying traffic, and emits no telemetry.

reference.label: Receiver degradation
reference.definition: Deterioration confined to one optical receiver that introduces errors without impairing the shared path.
reference.example: One coherent receiver reports high pre-FEC errors while another receiver on the same path remains normal.

reference.label: Laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive transmitter-laser wear that requires increasing bias current before eventual failure.
reference.example: Laser bias current rises to 123% of its beginning-of-life value while output is maintained.

reference.label: Channel margin erosion
reference.definition: Gradual reduction of an optical channel's remaining performance margin.
reference.example: Estimated channel margin declines from 4 dB to 2 dB over several months.

reference.label: Fibre break
reference.definition: A physical discontinuity in an optical fibre that interrupts light propagation.
reference.example: A cable cut leaves the next line amplifier with no input light.

reference.label: Complete amplifier failure
reference.definition: Total failure of an optical amplifier, resulting in no amplified output for any traversing channel.
reference.example: An inline amplifier goes dark and all downstream wavelengths disappear.

reference.label: Amplifier pump-laser failure
reference.definition: Failure of an amplifier's pump laser that prevents amplification despite input light being present.
reference.example: A preamplifier receives the WDM signal but produces no output after its pump fails.

reference.label: Amplifier unit failure
reference.definition: Non-pump hardware failure of an amplifier unit that leaves it unable to produce output.
reference.example: An amplifier power-supply fault causes a dark output despite valid input light.
synonyms: failure of the amplifier unit itself

reference.label: Disconnected optical jumper
reference.definition: Disconnection of an optical patch lead that opens the attached optical path.
reference.example: A technician removes the preamplifier input jumper and the multiplex-section input becomes dark.

reference.label: WSS ingress-port failure
reference.definition: Failure or blockage of one WSS ingress that stops all channels from its ROADM degree.
reference.example: The east-degree WSS input fails while channels from other degrees continue normally.

reference.label: Excessive fibre loss
reference.definition: Abnormally high attenuation on a fibre span that weakens or removes the received optical signal.
reference.example: A damaged splice adds 10 dB of loss and drives the downstream channel below its operating margin.

reference.label: Amplifier noise degradation
reference.definition: Increased noise contribution from an amplifier that reduces downstream OSNR despite possible normal output power.
reference.example: An amplifier maintains output power but reduces every channel's OSNR by 3 dB.

reference.label: Differential group-delay increase
reference.definition: Increased differential group delay that impairs coherent signal recovery.
reference.example: DGD rises to 35 ps and the receiver loses OTU frame alignment.

reference.label: WSS passband misalignment
reference.definition: Shift or narrowing of a WSS passband relative to a channel, reducing quality without necessarily reducing measured power.
reference.example: A WSS filter shifts 4 GHz from the carrier and causes errors while channel power remains nominal.

reference.label: Fast polarization event
reference.definition: A rapid state-of-polarization change that exceeds coherent-receiver tracking capability.
reference.example: Fibre movement produces a polarization-rate spike and a brief burst of errored seconds.

reference.label: Contaminated optical connector
reference.definition: Connector contamination that adds loss or reflection sufficient to impair an optical signal.
reference.example: Dust on a line connector raises pre-FEC BER above the signal-degrade threshold.

reference.label: Unspecified failure
reference.definition: A deliberately broad cause standing for any underlying failure capable of producing the associated status.
reference.example: Protection activation is attributed to an unspecified working-path failure until diagnosis is complete.

reference.label: Generic equipment failure
reference.definition: An unspecified equipment hardware failure where the affected component class is known but the mechanism is not.
reference.example: A card alarm identifies hardware failure without distinguishing a processor fault from a power fault.

reference.label: Amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: Partial loss of optical-amplifier gain that lowers output and degrades carried channels.
reference.example: An amplifier configured for 20 dB delivers only 17 dB and raises a gain-out-of-range alarm.

reference.label: Pump ageing
reference.definition: Progressive deterioration of an amplifier pump that requires increasing drive current to maintain gain.
reference.example: Pump current climbs to 121% of its beginning-of-life value while gain remains on target.

reference.label: Gain tilt
reference.definition: A wavelength-dependent amplifier gain imbalance that leaves channels near one band edge weaker than others.
reference.example: High-frequency edge channels leave an amplifier 3 dB below central channels.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: Failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric that interrupts ODUs traversing the switch.
reference.example: A fabric ASIC failure stops every cross-connected ODU and causes downstream AIS.

reference.label: Wrong ODU cross-connection
reference.definition: An erroneous ODU cross-connect that routes one ODU to an unintended endpoint.
reference.example: An ODU intended for client port 2 is provisioned to client port 7.

reference.label: Client-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a client-facing port or its optic that makes the associated client service unavailable.
reference.example: A 100GE client optic fails and its customer service goes down.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: Unintended gradual increase in WSS attenuation that lowers the power of a routed wavelength.
reference.example: A WSS setting drifts from 3 dB to 6 dB and its channel leaves the ROADM weak.

reference.label: No received light
reference.definition: Absence of detectable optical energy at an expected receiver input.
reference.example: After a fibre cut, received power falls below detection and the receiver declares loss of signal.

reference.label: Digital loss of signal
reference.definition: The digital loss-of-signal defect asserted when a receiver cannot detect a valid incoming signal.
reference.example: A dark line input causes the receiver to assert dLOS.

reference.label: OTU frame loss
reference.definition: Inability of a receiver to acquire or maintain valid OTU framing.
reference.example: Severe DGD prevents OTU header recognition and frame alignment is lost.

reference.label: OTU frame loss with light present
reference.definition: Loss of OTU framing while optical power remains detectable, indicating severe quality impairment rather than total signal absence.
reference.example: Received power remains −10 dBm but a shifted passband prevents OTU frame recovery.

reference.label: Card failed state
reference.definition: Observed state in which an equipment card is nonfunctional because of a card-level fault.
reference.example: A line card fails self-test and enters the card-failed state.

reference.label: Signal-quality equipment defect
reference.definition: A dEQ usage denoting received signal quality below the equipment's acceptable threshold.
reference.example: Excess decoder errors cause a receiver to assert quality dEQ before frame loss.

reference.label: Internal-equipment defect
reference.definition: A dEQ usage denoting an internally detected unit-level hardware failure.
reference.example: A failed FPGA self-test causes the card to assert equipment dEQ.

reference.label: Traffic-alarm masking
reference.definition: Suppression or obscuring of subordinate traffic alarms by a dominant equipment alarm.
reference.example: After card failure is declared, derivative OTU and ODU alarms from that card are masked.

reference.label: Received optical-signal degradation
reference.definition: A received signal remains present but has reduced power, OSNR, dispersion tolerance, filtering margin, or receiver margin.
reference.example: Light remains present, but low OSNR causes rising pre-FEC errors.

reference.label: Pre-FEC error degradation
reference.definition: Pre-correction errors appearing or exceeding a configured degradation threshold.
reference.example: Pre-FEC BER rises to 2×10^-3 and triggers signal degrade.

reference.label: Untrackable polarization change
reference.definition: Polarization variation whose rate exceeds the receiver's tracking capability.
reference.example: Mechanical vibration rotates polarization too quickly and briefly disrupts coherent recovery.

reference.label: Errored second
reference.definition: A one-second interval containing at least one counted transmission error.
reference.example: A polarization transient produces errors during 12 separate seconds.

reference.label: ODU-AIS insertion
reference.definition: Insertion of ODU alarm-indication signal downstream as a consequent action for an upstream defect.
reference.example: On OTU frame loss, the receiver inserts ODU-AIS into every contained ODU.

reference.label: Backward defect indication transmission
reference.definition: Transmission of a backward defect indication toward the remote transmitter after a receive-side defect.
reference.example: A receiver that loses OTU framing returns BDI to the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: Monitoring silence
reference.definition: Absence of telemetry, supervision, or performance reports from an affected unit.
reference.example: After a card loses power, its counters and status reports stop updating.

reference.label: Receiver-local errors
reference.definition: Transmission errors confined to one receiver rather than shared by the path or other channels.
reference.example: One receiver reports errors while a parallel receiver on the same signal remains clean.

reference.label: Unaffected normal state
reference.definition: Continued operation within limits outside the specifically affected component, channel, or degree.
reference.example: A west-degree ingress fails while east- and south-degree traffic remains normal.

reference.label: Far-end defect report
reference.definition: A backward indication that the remote endpoint detected a defect on the locally transmitted signal.
reference.example: The local terminal reports BDI after the remote receiver loses framing.

reference.label: Detected transmit-laser fault
reference.definition: A local diagnostic state indicating a fault in a transmitter laser or its drive circuitry.
reference.example: Laser supervision detects drive current but no output and declares a transmit fault.

reference.label: Detected card hardware fault
reference.definition: An internally detected hardware defect affecting an equipment card as a whole.
reference.example: A failed card power rail is detected during self-test.

reference.label: Laser-bias high threshold
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current above 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: An LBC reading of 123% satisfies the laser-ageing threshold.

reference.label: Constant-gain amplifier operation
reference.definition: Amplifier control that adjusts pump drive to maintain a configured optical gain.
reference.example: An amplifier increases pump current after input power falls to retain 20 dB gain.

reference.label: Provisioned amplifier gain target
reference.definition: The configured amplifier gain value against which actual gain is controlled and assessed.
reference.example: A booster is provisioned for 18 dB gain to compensate for its associated span.

reference.label: Reduced amplifier input power
reference.definition: A reduction in aggregate optical power entering an amplifier or optical unit.
reference.example: Added span loss reduces amplifier input power by 3 dB.

reference.label: Low optical output power
reference.definition: Optical output power below its expected level for one channel or a composite signal.
reference.example: An amplifier output is 4 dB below target and its carried wavelengths are correspondingly weak.

reference.label: Reduced OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio below its expected value on one or more channels.
reference.example: Every wavelength loses 2 dB of OSNR after amplifier degradation.

reference.label: No optical output
reference.definition: Absence of emitted optical light from an amplifier or transmission unit.
reference.example: A failed inline amplifier has no measurable output light.

reference.label: All carried channels lost
reference.definition: Simultaneous absence of every wavelength traversing a failed common optical element.
reference.example: Complete amplifier failure removes all 80 downstream channels.

reference.label: OSC not received
reference.definition: Failure to detect or decode the optical supervisory channel on a fibre section.
reference.example: A span cut causes the next amplifier site to report that OSC is not received.

reference.label: Section-local OSC failure
reference.definition: OSC loss limited to one section because each intermediate site terminates and regenerates the supervisory channel.
reference.example: OSC loss on span A–B does not suppress the independently launched OSC on span B–C.
synonyms: OSC failure confined to one span

reference.label: Rising pump drive current
reference.definition: An upward pump-current trend as amplifier control compensates for deterioration and preserves gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises from 100% to 118% while amplifier gain remains stable.

reference.label: Traffic maintained during pump ageing
reference.definition: Continued traffic service while pump-current headroom still allows the amplifier to meet its gain target.
reference.example: At 115% pump current, all channels remain error-free because target gain is maintained.
synonyms: traffic unaffected while gain is maintained

reference.label: Incipient ageing warning
reference.definition: A trend-based warning of developing component deterioration before traffic is disrupted.
reference.example: A sustained rise in pump current warns of pump ageing months before failure.

reference.label: Pump end-of-life threshold
reference.definition: Pump drive current above 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: Pump current reaches 122% and satisfies the end-of-life criterion.

reference.label: Band-edge channels weak
reference.definition: A subset of wavelengths near one spectral edge has lower power than central channels.
reference.example: Five high-frequency channels arrive 3 dB weaker than the rest.
synonyms: channels low at one band edge

reference.label: Input light present with no output
reference.definition: Amplifier failure signature in which input optical power is present but output is dark.
reference.example: The preamplifier reads −18 dBm at its input and no detectable output.
synonyms: light at input but none at output

reference.label: Amplifier gain out of range
reference.definition: Measured amplifier gain differing from its configured target by more than 2 dB.
reference.example: Measured gain is 17.5 dB against a 20 dB set point.
synonyms: gain more than 2 dB from target

reference.label: ODU-AIS received
reference.definition: Receipt of the standardized ODU alarm-indication pattern in place of valid upstream payload.
reference.example: A client port receives ODU-AIS after an upstream OTU loses frame.

reference.label: ODU-AIS forwarding
reference.definition: Propagation of received or generated ODU-AIS through each affected ODU cross-connection.
reference.example: An OTN switch carries AIS onward on every affected ODU egress.

reference.label: Misdirected ODU
reference.definition: An ODU delivered from an unexpected source or to an unintended endpoint.
reference.example: A port expecting CUSTOMER_A receives an ODU carrying CUSTOMER_B's trail trace.

reference.label: Client service unavailable
reference.definition: Loss of availability of a customer-facing service.
reference.example: A failed 100GE optic makes the associated customer circuit unavailable.

reference.label: Protected service configuration
reference.definition: A service arrangement with working and protection ODU paths available to a receive-side selector.
reference.example: A 100GE service is carried on two diverse ODU branches terminating at one selector.

reference.label: Defect-free protection path available
reference.definition: Availability of at least one selectable protection branch without a detected defect.
reference.example: The working ODU has AIS, so the selector chooses the clean protection ODU.

reference.label: Protection-switching hit
reference.definition: A short service interruption limited to the interval required to switch protection paths.
reference.example: Traffic drops for 35 ms while the selector changes to the protection branch.

reference.label: All traversing ODUs interrupted
reference.definition: Simultaneous traffic interruption of every ODU crossing a failed switch fabric.
reference.example: A fabric reset stops all ODUs routed through the switch.

reference.label: No optical-layer symptom
reference.definition: Normal optical power and quality despite a logical ODU-routing defect.
reference.example: A misrouted ODU has normal power and OSNR but fails its trail-trace check.

reference.label: Client-port failed state
reference.definition: Observed nonfunctional state of a client port or its associated optic.
reference.example: A 400GE pluggable stops operating and its port is marked failed.

reference.label: ODU backward-defect report
reference.definition: An ODU-layer backward report that the remote endpoint is receiving ODU-AIS or another trail defect.
reference.example: The remote endpoint receives AIS and returns ODU-BDI.

reference.label: ODU trail-trace mismatch
reference.definition: Received ODU trail identity differs from the identity provisioned at the termination.
reference.example: The expected trace is CUSTOMER_A but the received trace is CUSTOMER_B.

reference.label: Protection path active
reference.definition: The service selector currently uses the protection ODU path instead of the working path.
reference.example: After working-path loss, the selector moves to the standby ODU.

reference.label: Protection path unavailable
reference.definition: The protection ODU path has failed or cannot provide recovery.
reference.example: A cut on the standby route leaves traffic on working but removes redundancy.

reference.label: Incoming line-wide impairment
reference.definition: An optical impairment shared by all channels on an incoming multiplexed line or ROADM degree.
reference.example: Every wavelength entering on the west degree has the same OSNR penalty.

reference.label: Per-channel continuation of line impairment
reference.definition: Persistence of a common ingress impairment on each wavelength after the node routes channels independently.
reference.example: West-ingress channels retain their OSNR penalty after being split across east and south egresses.
synonyms: line impairment continues on routed channels

reference.label: Optical power re-levelling
reference.definition: Adjustment of an incoming channel back to its configured power target by a node.
reference.example: A channel arriving 5 dB low leaves the ROADM at nominal power.

reference.label: Residual OSNR penalty after re-levelling
reference.definition: Persistence of upstream-created OSNR degradation after optical power is restored.
reference.example: The node restores channel power, but the earlier 3 dB OSNR loss remains.

reference.label: Loss beyond levelling range
reference.definition: An upstream attenuation greater than the node's available power-correction range.
reference.example: A 12 dB loss exceeds an 8 dB levelling range, so the outgoing channel remains weak.

reference.label: Impairment pass-through
reference.definition: Propagation of an input property or impairment through a node without its removal.
reference.example: An incoming OSNR penalty remains after the wavelength crosses the ROADM.

reference.label: Normal optical power despite impairment
reference.definition: Measured channel power within its expected range even though another quality impairment exists.
reference.example: A passband-shifted channel has nominal power but elevated pre-FEC BER.

reference.label: Reduced signal quality
reference.definition: Reduced recoverability or margin of an optical signal independently of its absolute power.
reference.example: A channel retains normal power but has lower Q-factor after WSS filtering.

reference.label: ROADM-degree blocked
reference.definition: All channels arriving on one ROADM degree are prevented from passing through the node.
reference.example: A failed east-degree WSS ingress blocks every wavelength arriving from the east.

reference.label: Received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a receiver input.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports −14.2 dBm received power.

reference.label: Errored-seconds count
reference.definition: Count of one-second intervals containing errors, commonly accumulated in 15-minute bins.
reference.example: The latest 15-minute bin records 12 errored seconds.

reference.label: Optical signal-to-noise ratio
reference.definition: The ratio of channel optical signal power to optical noise power.
reference.example: Monitoring estimates the channel OSNR as 18.7 dB.

reference.label: Pre-FEC bit-error ratio
reference.definition: Bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction.
reference.example: The receiver reports a pre-FEC BER of 1.6×10^-3.

reference.label: Differential group delay
reference.definition: Measured differential delay between polarization modes of a coherent optical signal.
reference.example: The receiver reports DGD of 28 ps during a fibre disturbance.

reference.label: State-of-polarization change rate
reference.definition: Measured rate of change of an optical signal's state of polarization.
reference.example: SOP rate spikes above the receiver's tracking limit during cable movement.

reference.label: Transmit-laser bias current
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: LBC reads 121%, indicating substantial laser ageing.

reference.label: Composite input power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power across all wavelengths entering an amplifier or optical unit.
reference.example: An inline amplifier reports −8 dBm total input power.

reference.label: Composite output power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power across all wavelengths leaving an amplifier or optical unit.
reference.example: A booster reports +20 dBm total output power.

reference.label: Pump-laser drive current
reference.definition: Amplifier pump current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: An ageing preamplifier reports pump current at 118%.

reference.label: OSC receiver status
reference.definition: Status indicating whether the optical supervisory channel is present and received at an input.
reference.example: An amplifier reports OSC presence=false after an upstream span cut.

reference.label: Client errored seconds
reference.definition: Client-side count of seconds containing errors, normally reported in 15-minute bins.
reference.example: A 100GE port reports four client errored seconds in the latest bin.

reference.label: Client unavailable seconds
reference.definition: Client-side count of seconds during which the service is unavailable.
reference.example: A failed port records 900 unavailable seconds in a complete 15-minute bin.

reference.label: Per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for each wavelength channel.
reference.example: An optical channel monitor reports channel 37 at −5.8 dBm.

reference.label: Transponder
reference.definition: An optical terminal that maps client traffic onto a line-side wavelength.
reference.example: A 400G transponder converts a client signal into one coherent optical channel.

reference.label: Muxponder
reference.definition: An optical terminal that aggregates multiple client signals onto a higher-rate line channel.
reference.example: A 400G muxponder combines four 100GE clients into one line wavelength.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A card providing OTN line transmission and reception for an OTU and its contained ODUs.
reference.example: A 400G OTN line card terminates one OTU carrying several ODUs.

reference.label: VA-TPD-400
reference.definition: The VA-specific 400G transponder product represented in model A.
reference.example: A VA-TPD-400 carries one coherent 400G wavelength.

reference.label: VA-MXP-200
reference.definition: The VA-specific 200G muxponder product represented in model A.
reference.example: A VA-MXP-200 aggregates client traffic onto a 200G optical line signal.

reference.label: VA-MXP-400
reference.definition: The VA-specific 400G muxponder product represented in model A.
reference.example: A VA-MXP-400 aggregates clients onto one 400G optical channel.

reference.label: VA-OTN-LC-200
reference.definition: The VA-specific 200G OTN line-card product represented in model A.
reference.example: A VA-OTN-LC-200 terminates a 200G OTN line signal.

reference.label: VA-OTN-LC-400
reference.definition: The VA-specific 400G OTN line-card product represented in model A.
reference.example: A VA-OTN-LC-400 terminates a 400G OTU.

reference.label: EDFA card
reference.definition: An erbium-doped fibre-amplifier unit that amplifies all wavelengths traversing it.
reference.example: An EDFA card maintains 20 dB gain across an 80-channel WDM signal.

reference.label: Booster amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the transmitting end of a multiplex section that sets launch power.
reference.example: A booster after the ROADM amplifies the outgoing WDM band before the fibre span.

reference.label: Line amplifier
reference.definition: An intermediate optical amplifier installed along a route to restore WDM signal power.
reference.example: A line amplifier at a midpoint hut boosts all wavelengths on the route.

reference.label: Preamplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the receiving end of a multiplex section before node reception.
reference.example: A preamplifier boosts the incoming WDM band before the destination ROADM.

reference.label: OTN cross-connect switch
reference.definition: An ODU-layer switching resource that cross-connects ODU trails independently of their optical carriers.
reference.example: An OTN switch connects an incoming ODU2 from a line card to client port 8.

reference.label: Client interface port
reference.definition: A client-facing service interface and associated electronics or optic.
reference.example: A 100GE client port maps a customer signal into an ODU.

reference.label: 10GE client port
reference.definition: A client interface specifically operating at 10 Gigabit Ethernet.
reference.example: A 10GE port accepts a customer signal for OTN mapping.

reference.label: 100GE client port
reference.definition: A client interface specifically operating at 100 Gigabit Ethernet.
reference.example: A 100GE port terminates a customer circuit on a muxponder.

reference.label: 400GE client port
reference.definition: A client interface specifically operating at 400 Gigabit Ethernet.
reference.example: A 400GE port receives a client signal for OTN transport.

reference.label: CDC ROADM
reference.definition: A reconfigurable optical node that independently routes wavelength channels through WSS elements.
reference.example: A CDC ROADM routes one wavelength east and another south from the same ingress degree.

reference.label: ROADM degree WSS
reference.definition: The wavelength-selective-switch module serving one directional degree of a ROADM.
reference.example: The west-degree WSS receives and routes all wavelengths arriving from the west.

reference.label: OCH_LOS
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that an optical-channel receiver detects no expected channel light.
reference.example: A fibre cut removes a wavelength and the receiver raises OCH_LOS.

reference.label: OTU_LOF
reference.definition: Alarm indicating loss of OTU frame alignment at a receiver.
reference.example: A severe passband fault prevents framing and raises OTU_LOF.

reference.label: OTU_SD
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that OTU pre-FEC errors exceed the configured degradation threshold.
reference.example: A dirty connector drives pre-FEC BER above threshold and raises OTU_SD.

reference.label: OTU_BDI
reference.definition: OTU indication that the far end detected a defect on the locally transmitted OTU.
reference.example: The local terminal reports OTU_BDI after its remote peer loses framing.

reference.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
reference.definition: Equipment alarm identifying a detected transmit-laser fault.
reference.example: No laser output despite drive current causes EQPT_TX_FAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
reference.definition: Equipment alarm identifying an internal card hardware fault.
reference.example: A failed card power rail causes EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: LASER_BIAS_HIGH
reference.definition: Incipient ageing alarm raised when transmit-laser bias exceeds its defined threshold.
reference.example: LASER_BIAS_HIGH is raised when LBC reaches 123%.

reference.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
reference.definition: Line-amplifier alarm indicating loss of incoming optical light.
reference.example: A cut ahead of an inline amplifier causes AMP_INPUT_LOS.

reference.label: OMS_LOS_P
reference.definition: Preamplifier alarm indicating loss of the incoming optical multiplex-section signal.
reference.example: Removing the receive-side jumper causes OMS_LOS_P.

reference.label: OSC_LOS
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that the span optical supervisory channel is not received.
reference.example: A feeding-span fault causes the next amplifier site to raise OSC_LOS.

reference.label: AMP_FAIL
reference.definition: Alarm raised when an amplifier has input light but produces no output.
reference.example: A failed pump leaves input illuminated and output dark, raising AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
reference.definition: Alarm raised when measured amplifier gain differs from its target by more than 2 dB.
reference.example: Actual gain of 17 dB against a 20 dB target raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

reference.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
reference.definition: Alarm indicating pump drive current has exceeded the defined end-of-life threshold.
reference.example: Pump current at 122% raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: CLIENT_SF
reference.definition: Client-port alarm indicating that the associated client service is unavailable.
reference.example: A switch-fabric failure removes a 100GE service and raises CLIENT_SF.

reference.label: ODU_AIS
reference.definition: Client-port indication that ODU alarm-indication signal has been received.
reference.example: An upstream OTU failure causes the client port to report ODU_AIS.

reference.label: ODU_BDI
reference.definition: Client-port indication that the far end has reported an ODU-layer defect.
reference.example: The remote endpoint receives AIS and returns ODU_BDI.

reference.label: ODU_TIM
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that the received ODU trail identity differs from the expected identity.
reference.example: A port expecting CUSTOMER_A receives CUSTOMER_B's trace and raises ODU_TIM.

reference.label: PROT_ACTIVE
reference.definition: Protection-state indication that service is currently selected from the protection path.
reference.example: Working-path failure causes the selector to switch and report PROT_ACTIVE.

reference.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
reference.definition: Protection-state alarm indicating that the protection path is unavailable for recovery.
reference.example: A cut on the standby path raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
reference.definition: Equipment alarm identifying a hardware fault in a client port or its optic.
reference.example: A failed 100GE port ASIC causes EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
reference.definition: Equipment alarm identifying a hardware fault in an OTN cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: A failed fabric ASIC raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL and interrupts traversing ODUs.

reference.label: Single optical channel
reference.definition: Exactly one wavelength channel, distinguished from neighboring channels on the same line.
reference.example: A transmitter failure removes its one 400G channel while other wavelengths remain present.

reference.label: All shared optical channels
reference.definition: Every wavelength sharing the affected line, amplifier, or other common element.
reference.example: A dead amplifier removes all channels traversing it.

reference.label: Channels on one ROADM degree
reference.definition: All wavelengths entering a ROADM through one directional degree.
reference.example: A failed north-degree ingress blocks every channel arriving from the north.
synonyms: all channels arriving on that degree

reference.label: Other ROADM degrees
reference.definition: Directional ROADM interfaces other than the specifically affected degree.
reference.example: East and south degrees remain operational when the west ingress fails.

reference.label: Single receiver
reference.definition: The individual receiving function under examination, excluding the shared path and other receivers.
reference.example: A photodiode fault causes errors at one receiver only.

reference.label: Optical path
reference.definition: The end-to-end optical route and common transmission elements carrying a channel.
reference.example: A dirty connector anywhere on the optical path can reduce received OSNR.

reference.label: All traversing ODUs
reference.definition: Every ODU whose route passes through the affected OTN switch fabric.
reference.example: A fabric outage interrupts all ODUs traversing the switch.

reference.label: Single ODU
reference.definition: One ODU trail or container rather than the complete set carried by a switch or OTU.
reference.example: A wrong cross-connect misroutes one ODU while the others remain correct.

reference.label: Client service
reference.definition: The customer-facing service carried through a client port and associated ODU path.
reference.example: A 100GE customer circuit is the client service lost after port failure.

reference.label: Far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote optical receiver terminating a channel sent by the local transmitter.
reference.example: A local laser failure appears as signal loss at the far-end receiver.

reference.label: Far-end endpoint
reference.definition: The remote termination of a monitored connection relative to the current observation point.
reference.example: The far end returns BDI after detecting a receive defect.

reference.label: Local equipment
reference.definition: The equipment instance currently reporting or undergoing diagnosis.
reference.example: Pump-current measurements identify ageing on the local amplifier.

reference.label: Upstream feeding span
reference.definition: The immediately upstream fibre section that supplies optical input to a unit.
reference.example: A break on the feeding span leaves the line-amplifier input dark.

reference.label: Preceding amplifier
reference.definition: The nearest upstream optical amplifier whose output feeds the current span or unit.
reference.example: Failure of the preceding amplifier causes loss of input at the next site.

reference.label: Downstream
reference.definition: The direction or network region following a point in the direction of signal flow.
reference.example: ODU-AIS is inserted downstream after OTU frame loss.

reference.label: Working ODU path
reference.definition: The primary ODU route normally selected for a protected service.
reference.example: A defect on the working path causes selection of protection.

reference.label: Protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU route available to protect a service.
reference.example: The selector chooses the protection path when the working ODU carries AIS.

reference.label: Standard monitoring availability
reference.definition: Monitoring functionality available by default on all applicable units.
reference.example: Applicable units report errored seconds without an optional monitoring licence.

reference.label: Power monitoring option
reference.definition: Optional capability enabling received, input, or output optical-power measurements.
reference.example: A licensed amplifier reports total input and output power.

reference.label: Advanced monitoring option
reference.definition: Optional capability enabling metrics such as OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, polarization rate, laser bias, or pump current.
reference.example: Advanced monitoring exposes pre-FEC BER and DGD on a coherent receiver.

reference.label: Channel monitoring option
reference.definition: Optional capability enabling per-wavelength power and channel OSNR measurements.
reference.example: A ROADM with channel monitoring reports power for every wavelength.

reference.label: Fifteen-minute performance bins
reference.definition: Reporting of performance counters as values accumulated over 15-minute intervals.
reference.example: Client ES and UAS are retrieved for the previous 15-minute interval.

reference.label: Hard failure
reference.definition: An abrupt, complete failure that removes signal, output, equipment operation, or service.
reference.example: A fibre cut instantly removes all received light.

reference.label: Degradation
reference.definition: An impairment that reduces quality or margin while some signal or service may remain available.
reference.example: A 3 dB OSNR decline raises errors without immediately interrupting traffic.

reference.label: Incipient condition
reference.definition: A developing precursor that indicates likely future component failure before immediate traffic impact.
reference.example: Rising pump current provides warning while amplifier gain is still maintained.

reference.label: Provisioning-associated fault
reference.definition: A fault pattern occurring mainly after configuration or cross-connect changes.
reference.example: ODU_TIM appears immediately after an operator provisions the ODU to the wrong egress.

reference.label: Critical severity
reference.definition: Highest alarm priority for immediate major service or equipment loss.
reference.example: Complete loss of an optical channel is assigned critical severity.

reference.label: Major severity
reference.definition: Serious alarm priority below critical for substantial faults requiring prompt attention.
reference.example: Loss of the supervisory channel may be assigned major severity while payload remains present.

reference.label: Minor severity
reference.definition: Lower alarm priority for warnings, degradations, or redundancy changes without immediate major loss.
reference.example: A pump end-of-life warning is assigned minor severity while traffic remains intact.

reference.label: Not-alarmed status
reference.definition: Informational classification for a reported indication that does not itself raise a severity alarm.
reference.example: A received ODU-AIS indication may be reported as not alarmed.

reference.label: G.798 OTU frame-loss actions
reference.definition: On OTU frame loss, insert ODU-AIS on every contained ODU and return BDI toward the far-end transmitter.
reference.example: Loss of framing causes AIS on three tributary ODUs and BDI toward the remote transmitter.

reference.label: Per-span OSC regeneration
reference.definition: Each amplifier site terminates the incoming OSC and originates a separate OSC on the next span.
reference.example: Site B receives the A–B OSC and independently launches the B–C OSC.

reference.label: SNCP receive-side selection
reference.definition: Protection using working and protection ODU copies with selection at the receiving client port.
reference.example: When the working ODU develops AIS, the receiver selects the defect-free protection copy.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM switching
reference.definition: ROADM forwarding in which each wavelength is independently selected and routed at an egress degree.
reference.example: A ROADM routes one incoming wavelength east and another south.

reference.label: OTN AIS transparency
reference.definition: An OTN switch carries ODU-AIS onward through the corresponding ODU cross-connections.
reference.example: AIS received on two ODUs is forwarded through both configured switch egresses.
